senses.gloss: to be void, abolished, suspended; to cease to exist.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 103b:14">Keth. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>בָּטְלָה קדושה</he> sanctity of life ceased; [oth. opin.: the levitical law concerning the contact with a corpse was suspended in favor of Rabbi; v. Tosaf. a. l.].
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:16">Ab. V, 16</cite> <he>ב׳ דבר בְּטֵלָה וכ׳</he> as soon as the (sensual) attraction disappears, love will disappear.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:21">Ib. 21</cite> as if dead <he>ועבר וב׳ מן העולם</he> and passed away and disappeared from this world.
Y. Meg. I, 70ᵈ top, a. e. בטלה מגלת תענית the Scroll of Fasts has been abolished (the festive commemorations enumerated therein are no more observed).
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 9:9">Sot. IX, 9</cite> (<cite ref="Sotah 47a:20">47ᵃ</cite>); a. fr.

senses.gloss: to rest from labor, be at ease, be idle.
units: <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 4:10">Ab. IV, 10</cite> <he>אם בָּטַלְתָּ מן וכ׳</he> if thou choosest not to study the law, there will be many disturbances (excuses) to assist thee.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:5">Ib. I, 5</cite> <he>בּוֹטֵל מד״ת</he> he neglects the study of the Law; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be abolished, suspended. Y. Meg. I, 70ᵈ bot. עתידין לִיבָּטֵל (= לְהִיבָּטֵל) shall in future be abolished (neglected).
units: <cite ref="Gittin 32a:11">Gitt. 32ᵃ</cite>, v. infra.

senses.gloss: to be excused, be exempt. Ib. II, 16 thou art not a free man להִבָּטֵל ממנה so as to be exempt from life’s duties.

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 4:5">Gitt. IV, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Gittin 41b:1">41ᵇ</cite>) <he>יִבָּטֵל</he> shall he never marry?

Ab. II, 4 בַּטֵּל רצונך וכ׳ set aside thy will for the sake of the Lord’s will, in order that He may set aside the will of others (euphem. for His will) for the sake of thy will (withdraw evil decrees at thy prayer).
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 4:9">Ib. IV, 9</cite> <he>המְבַטֵּל וכ׳</he> he who neglects the study of the Law on account of his wealth.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 9:10">Sot. IX, 10</cite> (<cite ref="Sotah 47a:20">47ᵃ</cite>) <he>אף הוא בִּטֵּל את המעוררין</he> he also abolished (the custom of) the wakers, v. <cite ref="P01454"><he>עָרַר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 63a:22">Sabb. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>מְבַטְּלָהּ</he> he (the observer of the Law) will cancel it (avert God’s evil decree). Mekh. B’shall., Amalek, 2, v. <cite ref="A01551"><he>אִיפָּטִיקוֹס</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Makkot 24a">Macc. 24ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 4:7">Ab. Zar. IV, 7</cite> <he>למה אינו מְבַטְּלָהּ</he> why does He not destroy it (the objects of idol worship)?—
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 4:1">Gitt. IV, 1</cite> <he>שוב אינו יכול לבַטְּלוֹ</he> he can no longer annul it (his letter of divorce).
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 4:2">Ib. 2</cite> in former times a man could summon a court in a strange place <he>ובִּטְּלוֹ</he> and declare it (the letter of divorce which he had sent off) void.
<cite ref="Gittin 32b:3">Ib. 32ᵇ</cite> <he>אתי דיבור ומבטל דיבור</he> a word (declaration) comes and cancels a word.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 4:4">Ab. Zar. IV, 4</cite> (<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 42b:2">42ᵇ</cite>) an idolator (gentile) <he>מבטל אליל שלו וכ׳</he> may (by mutilation &c.) cancel his own or his neigbor’s idol (so that it is no longer subject to the law forbidding Jews to derive any benefits from idolatrous paraphernalia), but an Israelite cannot &c.

Ib. המב׳ אליל ב׳ וכ׳ in cancelling an idol, one has at the same time cancelled its attachments; a. fr.—ב׳ רשות to resign possession, a legal fiction by which the carrying of objects on the Sabbath from one’s own place to one common to several persons, may be permitted.

<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 6:7">Erub. VI, 7</cite> <he>מְבַטֵּל את רשותו</he> he (the brother who forgot to lay the Erub, v. <cite ref="P00680"><he>עֵירוּב</he></cite>) must resign his share in the common property.

<cite ref="Eruvin 68b:1">Ib. 68ᵇ</cite> <he>מבטלין וחוזרין ומב׳</he> you may resign your share to your neighbor, and then he may resign to you; a. fr.—<he>ב׳ חמץ</he> to renounce (by declaration) the possession of anything leavened that may have remained undiscovered in one’s possession.
Pes. 6ᵇ הבודק צריך שיְבַטֵּל after one has searched the house for leavened things, he must renounce (whatever he may have failed to find); a. fr.—Part. pass. מְבוּטָּל, f. מְבוּטֶּלֶת.
<cite ref="Eruvin 69b:14">Erub. 69ᵇ</cite> <he>רשותי מב׳ לך</he> my possession be resigned to thee (for Sabbath purposes).

<cite ref="Gittin 32a:11">Gitt. 32ᵃ</cite> if a recipient says, <he>מתנה זו מב׳</he> ‘this donation be void’, <he>תִּיבָּטֵל</he> ‘shall be void’, opp. to <he>בְּטֵלָה היא</he> ‘is a void one’, i.e. has been annulled.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 1:5">Eduy. I, 5</cite>; <cite ref="Gittin 36b">Gitt. 36ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אין ב״ד יכול לבַ׳ וכ׳</he> no court can repeal (overrule) the decisions of another court, unless &c.

senses.gloss: to neutralize an admixture of forbidden food &c. in a certain quantity.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 108a:8">Ḥull. 108ᵃ</cite> <he>ושאינו מינו … ומבטלו</he> and the portion of the mixture which is not its kind is prevailing and neutralizes the forbidden portion (as if did not exist at all); a. fr.
<cite ref="Eruvin 63b">Erub. 63ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Megillah 3a:21">Meg. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>בִּיטַּלְתֶּם וכ׳</he> ye interfered with the daily offering; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:5">Ber. II, 5</cite> <he>לבטל ממני וכ׳</he> to suspend (shake off) the yoke of heavenly government even one minute.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 5:5">Succ. V, 5</cite> <he>להַבְטִיל את העם וכ׳</he> to cause the people to cease working.

senses.gloss: to be interrupted &c., v. Nif.—Tan. d’be El. I, 5; II, 3.
